name: christopherdavenport
description: Chris Davenport's personal Claude Code skills and agents.

plugins.name: financial-accounting
plugins.description: ~109 tok always-on. Financial institution accounting fundamentals (journals, ledgers, sub-ledgers, chart of accounts) and US GAAP (FASB ASC) reference for FI operations.

plugins.name: financial-regs
plugins.description: ~106 tok always-on. US financial regulation lookup and compliance analysis.

plugins.name: lit
plugins.description: ~96 tok always-on. Lit web component library expertise.

plugins.name: jh-design-system
plugins.description: ~89 tok always-on. Jack Henry Design System (jackhenry.design/v2) — components, foundations, tokens, content.

plugins.name: go
plugins.description: ~52 tok always-on. Go language best practices — Effective Go, Google + Uber style guides, Code Review Comments, modern stdlib (errors, context, slog, generics).

plugins.name: spanner
plugins.description: ~90 tok always-on. Google Cloud Spanner best practices — schema design, interleaving, indexes, transactions, query/DML optimization, schema evolution, and the Go client SDK.

plugins.name: sqlite
plugins.description: ~97 tok always-on. SQLite best practices — STRICT tables, the must-set pragmas (WAL, busy_timeout, foreign_keys, synchronous=NORMAL), BEGIN IMMEDIATE vs DEFERRED, indexes and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, JSON1/JSONB with generated-column indexing, the Go client (database/sql with mattn/go-sqlite3 or modernc.org/sqlite), and server-side production use (Litestream/LiteFS/Turso/D1).

plugins.name: pubsub
plugins.description: ~72 tok always-on. Google Cloud Pub/Sub best practices — topics & schemas, subscription types, delivery guarantees, ordering, dead-letter, ack deadline / lease, publisher batching, and the Go client SDK.

plugins.name: typescript
plugins.description: ~114 tok always-on. TypeScript best practices — type system, generics, utility & advanced types, discriminated unions, classes & OOP, error handling, async & cancellation, immutability, modules, strict tsconfig, naming, testing, plus a dedicated section on functional patterns.

plugins.name: commit-story
plugins.description: ~201 tok always-on. Take a batch of uncommitted work and split it into a sequence of meaningful commits with reviewer-grade messages, while guaranteeing the final tree is byte-identical to the starting tree. Plans the commit sequence, presents it for approval, executes whole-file or hunk-level splits via git apply --cached, and verifies the result with diff and tree-hash comparisons. Snapshots the baseline as a stash up front so any failure can be safely rolled back.

plugins.name: excalidraw
plugins.description: ~250 tok always-on. Read, create, and edit Excalidraw (.excalidraw) diagrams as data — inspect/summarize, generate schema-valid diagrams and flowcharts, add/move/restyle/connect shapes with bound arrows and labels, convert simple Mermaid, and validate. Not for rasterizing PNG/SVG in-process.

plugins.name: pr-description
plugins.description: ~193 tok always-on. Write a PR title and body a reviewer can act on in under a minute, sized to the change and to whatever pull-request template the repo ships. Sources facts from the diff rather than the commit log, requires a 15–60 word lead before the first heading, holds the body to a measured density budget tiered on diff size, and moves the record of how the work went into a follow-up comment instead of the body. Ships a scorer the skill runs on its own draft before presenting it. Not for splitting work into commits (that is commit-story), reviewing code, or merging.

plugins.name: github-twin
plugins.description: ~0 tok always-on. Personal RAG over your GitHub history (commits, code, review comments), served to Claude Code over MCP. Provides find_code, find_reviews, predict_review_outcome, house_rules, developer_profile, and related tools.

plugins.name: claude-local-telemetry
plugins.description: ~109 tok always-on. Local observability for Claude Code. An OTLP/HTTP-JSON sink, a backfill that imports the transcripts already on disk, an MCP server and a dashboard, all over one SQLite file — so you can ask what your sessions cost, what tools ran, which agents and workflows the work was delegated to, and whether your hooks are actually firing, without sending telemetry anywhere. Node 24, no collector, loopback only.

plugins.name: guardrails
plugins.description: ~404 tok always-on. Containment policy for agentic sessions, built on Claude Code's OS-level sandbox rather than around it. Ships a sandbox-policy skill (settings keys, scope rules that silently ignore misplaced keys, four validated policy templates, failure modes), /guardrails-setup to generate and install a policy this repo's build actually survives, and /guardrails-doctor to check what is enforced rather than what is configured. Three hooks cover the gaps the sandbox leaves: credential shapes in outbound MCP and WebFetch payloads, Bash calls that opt out with dangerouslyDisableSandbox, an audit log, and an opt-in Stop gate that refuses to let an agent finish on a red build. A plugin cannot ship permissions or sandbox settings — only the means to write them into a scope the harness honours.
